name: push-based-host-burn-alert
title: Push-based host long-thread burn detection: doctor burn scan plus usage_sweep --alert
description: B-70e9 (DONE, v0.3.184) shipped the read-only `lattice usage_sweep` retro-attribution report, which successfully attributed a 1.76B-cumulative-input month-old Codex Desktop thread (rollout 019e40d0, ~/.codex/sessions/2026/05/19/, 13,648 turns, per-turn prompt grown 47k->247k) plus 9 concurrently-open proofbound desktop threads. But the sweep is PULL-based: it only detects runaway host threads when someone remembers to run it. Interactive desktop threads re-send their entire accumulated context every turn (a doc read once gets re-paid every subsequent turn - the 019e40d0 thread re-paid one execution-plan doc 1251 times), so early LOUD detection is the only lever lattice has for sessions it did not launch. This story makes detection PUSH-based: (1) a `lattice doctor` advisory check that reuses the core/usage-sweep.ts scanners (read-only) and flags host sessions exceeding env-tunable thresholds (transcript file size, cumulative input tokens, session age with recent activity), printing a prominent warning naming the session file, cwd, and cumulative tokens; (2) a `usage_sweep --alert` mode that exits non-zero when any session exceeds thresholds, so a cron job can drive notifications. Both surfaces stay advisory-only: no gate, gateEvidence=false, consistent with B-70e9 non-goals (desktop sessions are report-only).
